scope.typedPrefixIdentities: Outside this annotation scope. Resolve the typed prefix through the identity-and-evidence section 3 identity table; its hex suffix is not a separate bare digest field.

x-opensip-payload-registry.standing: Normative closed registry for every registered PAYLOAD in this graph. It resolves the question a payload schema digest alone cannot: which document bytes are hashed and which selector validates. It is the single mapping identity-and-evidence section 3 names; nothing in this graph admits a payload under a caller-chosen or guessed schema.

law.payloadSchemaDigest: raw SHA-256 of the EXACT FULL schema DOCUMENT file bytes named by the row
law.validation: by the row SELECTOR against that document, resolved through the pinned local registry closure with no network retrieval. A payload is NEVER validated against a whole multi-record bundle, and a bundle is never required to carry a root type: the row, not the document shape, decides admission.
law.codec: C (section 3 canonical JSON) for every class below
law.unregistered: a key with no row refuses; there is no default row and no caller-selected schema
law.keyedBy: a key name prefixed `payload.` is read from the parsed payload; every other name is read from the naming record. The key is never caller-selected free text.

relation.note: The 13 rows live in the document itself so relation, selector, universe rule and rung ladder cannot drift from the schemas they describe. fact.resolution must be a rung of the row ladder, the rung required/forbidden field rules apply, and universeRule same-only requires fact.sourceUniverse == fact.targetUniverse.

import.note: The Run closure re-derives these rows from the workflow registry and refuses if they differ, so one registry cannot drift from the other.

workflows/schemas/policy-document.schema.note: The workflow glob scope-policy document that comparison-result EvaluationContext.scopeDigest names and that the comparison contract requires to be bound as an analysis-spec parameter. With the class closed to one document that binding refused at Plan admission, so the comparison scope axis could not be populated at all. This row is deliberately a DIFFERENT record from the foundation scope-descriptor that plan.scopeDigest names: scope-descriptor is the repository extent actually walked (workspace roots and path prefixes), ScopeDocumentV1 is the policy's include/exclude glob selection over that extent. Both may appear in one Plan; neither substitutes for the other.

foundation/enumeration-plan.schema.v1.js.note: Exactly one required enumeration-plan parameter for the version3 evaluator. Independent pre-Plan selection; no parent PlanId or analysisSpecDigest self-reference.

foundation/evaluator-emission-plan.schem.note: Exactly one for evaluator3; explicit per-rule selected detector binding.

parameter.note: An analysis-spec or stage-spec parameter may only cite a document on this closed list. That replaces the withdrawn "a payload schema document must constrain the payload directly" rule, which contradicted the native and workflow bundle registries. A cited schema with no row refuses: there is no default row, no caller-selected schema and no permissive fallback for an unregistered parameter.

selectionCardinality.law: ONE Plan selects AT MOST ONE parameter per registered row. Zero is legal for a row this analysis does not need; two or more entries of analysis-spec.parameters (or stage-spec.parameters) whose schemaDigest resolves to the SAME row are REFUSED, whatever their payloadDigests are. This is a SELECTION rule about how many entries a SPEC may carry and is a different question from keyIsTheDocumentNotThePair, which is about how many REGISTRY ROWS one document digest may resolve to; PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW answers the second and never constrained the first.
selectionCardinality.why: A parameter row is a Plan INPUT: the payload it cites is the value the analysis is run with. Two entries under one row put two different values in one input slot and nothing decides which is the Plan's. Both enter analysisSpecDigest and therefore PlanId, so two conforming hosts could bind different documents from ONE admitted Plan and the resulting comparison axis would attribute differently for the same PlanId. Refusing is the registry declining an arbitrary selection, exactly as it does for an ambiguous row. There is deliberately NO default, NO first-listed or last-listed winner, and NO merge.
selectionCardinality.zeroIsLegal: An ordinary analysis that does not need a scope-policy input selects no ScopeDocumentV1 parameter and closes. A caller that DOES need it - baseline adoption and comparison - still gets the explicit missing-selection refusal from the workflow binding verifier; absence is never silently substituted, and the foundation scope-descriptor named by plan.scopeDigest is a DIFFERENT record that never stands in for ScopeDocumentV1.
selectionCardinality.exactDuplicatesAreADifferentRefusal: Two BYTE-IDENTICAL parameter entries are a malformed record, not an ambiguous selection: analysis-spec.parameters is uniqueItems with x-opensip-order canonical-set, so a whole-item duplicate refuses on the schema and on the collection order law (ORDER_OR_DUPLICATE) before any selection question is asked. This rule owns only the case those cannot see: DISTINCT entries citing one row.
enforcedAt: the PRE-PLAN analysis-spec admission boundary (native_evidence_model.admit_analysis_spec, after schema and vocabulary admission)
retained Run closure over the retained analysis-spec (identity-model close_run, ANALYSIS_SPEC_PARAMETER_SELECTION_AMBIGUOUS)
independently in the bounded workflow scope binding verifier when it is called directly (workflows_model.verify_scope_parameter_binding)
selectionCardinality.precedence: MOST SPECIFIC FIRST. The import-source-context row keeps its own named guard IMPORT_SOURCE_CONTEXT_MULTIPLE where that guard runs - inside the Run-closure import derivation, which is the boundary that consumes the row - and this generic selection guard is the TOTAL backstop that runs for every row and every Plan, including one with no selected import. Nothing about the import row's zero/one/multiple rule changes: zero means an empty declared-build set, one is the selection, more than one is refused.
selectionCardinality.notAStageSpecDuplicate: A stage-spec carries a SUBSET of the Plan analysis-spec parameters (STAGE_SPEC_HIDDEN_PARAMETER), so a Plan admitted under this rule cannot contain a stage that selects a row twice; the stage-spec case is implied rather than separately guarded, and stating that is not a claim that a second guard exists.

parameter.keyIsTheDocumentNotThePair: Normative accounting of a bounded limitation, retained deliberately (CB4-ADV-4). The key is the cited schemaDigest, which is the SHA-256 of the whole DOCUMENT's bytes, not a (document, selector) pair. Both rows are distinguishable today - import-source-context.schema.json and policy-document.schema.json are different documents with different digests - so there is no ambiguity in this release. The limitation is structural and is stated rather than left to be rediscovered: a SECOND parameter row selecting another $def out of a document an existing row already cites would be indistinguishable by this key, and the first listed would otherwise silently win. That case is FORBIDDEN and refuses (PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW), which is the registry law declining to make an arbitrary selection rather than a defect. Note that the same policy-document.schema.json bytes are also named by plan.policyDigest and plan.waiverDigest, but under the `canonical-record` representation and a different payload CLASS, so those are not in this key space and raise no collision.
parameter.whyNotRekeyByDocumentAndSelector: Re-keying the class by (document, selector) would lift the restriction and would change no identity today, and it is deliberately NOT done here. No existing requirement needs a second $def out of one document as a parameter; adding flexibility no requirement asks for would widen the closed key space and the admission surface for a case that does not exist, and would retire an explicit refusal in exchange for a rule that has never been exercised. If such a requirement ever arises it is an explicit versioned design correction with its own controls - not a silent widening, and not something an implementer may assume.

x-opensip-evaluator-profile.standing: Selected evaluator3 contract; source acceptance and product qualification are recorded separately.
x-opensip-evaluator-profile.majorLaw: Changed output domains dispatch explicitly to version3 records and prefixes. Frozen version2 bytes remain historical; no coercion or permissive mixed-version parse. Unchanged ancestors referenced by digest retain their existing identifier majors; their values change if committed input/schema bytes change.
x-opensip-evaluator-profile.integrationStatus: Public identity-model.v3.close_run performs owner/native/schema admission and complete evaluator replay, including retained execution-input totality. Workflow and security adapters consume this boundary. Synthetic reference graphs do not qualify a compiler, host, platform or release.

x-opensip-evaluator-deficiency-registry.causeLaw: Source-specific closed membership; evidenceKind is required for import and null otherwise, nativeCause is an owner NativeCause carrier or null. Gating derives from policy evidenceUse / required execution cells. Unknown record shape is refused, never coerced to a cause.
x-opensip-evaluator-deficiency-registry.importKindLaw: Exact atom evidence kind or independently assessed evidenceUse declaration; absence has no importId but still has an evidenceKind.

Identity3RuleEnumeration.description: Retained OUTPUT recomputed from Plan-bound expected inventories and rule selection. Incomplete includes unavailable and partial population or unknown export membership. Complete-empty is explicit. Disabled is all arrays empty. Inventory refs include all relevant expected outcomes, including unavailable records; unseen population never gets a fabricated subject id.

Identity3RuleResult.description: One result for EVERY compiled policy rule, including disabled and zero-subject rules, strictly sorted by ruleId. Outcome is recomputed after explicit waiver resolution and effective gate selection; advisory matches remain findings with pass sealed rule outcome. Enumeration uncertainty survives waived known findings.

budget.description: The deterministic analysis budget. identity-and-evidence section 3 requires plan.budget to equal this value exactly and by type; an override is made here first so both committed places agree.

importIds.description: Exactly the Plan-selected import set of this Run's Plan, repeated: equal as a canonical set to plan.importIds (IMPORT_JOIN). A repetition of the selection, never a second selection. This array is not an evaluated subset and is not proof.evaluationInputRefs (that field is the complete selectedRefs plus the execution-inputs ref). A selected import that nothing evaluated is still resolved and retained by the Run closure, and being selected alone grants it no evidence authority. Matched and uncertain observation addresses live on predicate-witness matchingImportRows/uncertainImportRows. Atomic predicateProofs[].inputRefs copy the whole evaluationInputRefs under composition §9.2 and therefore may list every selected import without those imports being consulted observation evidence.

Identity3SourceInventory.description: The snapshot source inventory as a registered record in its own right, so that vcs-observation.sourceInventoryDigest names a record rather than an unnamed canonical fragment.

Identity3StageSpec.description: The closed record digested by stageSpecDigest. execution-plan.stages[].stageSpecDigest and cache-key.stageSpecDigest are the SAME field name because they are the same digest of the same record under the same recipe; there are not two recipes for one spelling.

x-opensip-vocabulary.authority: The versioned semantic interface of stage-spec.producerClosure, implemented by the retained selected closure.
x-opensip-vocabulary.scope: Provider-defined logical operation tokens, not a platform-wide enum or host-selected physical-plan labels.
x-opensip-vocabulary.admission: Text validates shape only. Stage execution/replay uses the selected producer interface and its declared parameter/output contract.

x-opensip-digest.artifact: the exact complete registered parameter schema document bytes

parameters.description: every row must also be a row of the Plan analysis-spec parameters: a stage takes no hidden input

x-opensip-vocabulary.meaning: Registered output-domain names; declaration alone grants no producer or evidence authority.

outputDomains.description: Declared output-domain set. Empty is permitted and asserts no output domains; it does not establish completeness or result authority. Stage and stage-spec sets must agree.

x-opensip-digest.artifact: the exact complete bytes of the stage output schema document REGISTERED BY this stage-spec's producerClosure: the member of that closure's tree at registeredBy.treePath

registeredBy.law: Retained bytes are not a registration. The producer interface that owns the operation owns its output schema, so the schema is registered exactly when the Plan-selected producer closure carries it at the tree path for that operation; a new operation is registered by shipping its interface document in the admitted closure, never by a host or platform table.

enumeratorClosure.description: The Plan-selected closure that enumerated this scope. Its kind must be 'provider': enumeration is a native provider act, and no 'enumerator' kind is minted for it. The closure must also be a member of plan.semanticClosures, so the enumerator is one the Plan selected.

x-opensip-digest.artifact: the exact complete bytes of a schema document on the closed x-opensip-payload-registry list, DECLARED by this view's producer as a schema this view admitted under. The set is the producer's declaration and not a derived union: it is neither required to name every document a member fact or Coverage was admitted under, nor forbidden from naming a registered document this view admitted nothing under. Each member fact and Coverage independently pins and retains its own document through its own payloadSchemaDigest, which is where payload admission is decided.

Imported1BuildIdentityV1.description: Closed preimage of wrapper.buildDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob).

Imported1HistoryPayloadV1.description: Payload domain workflow.import-payload.history.v1. Advisory priority input only.

Imported1ImportObservationV1.description: Closed preimage of wrapper.observationDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob). Null members mean the observation semantics do not apply to the kind.

Imported1ImportScopeDescriptor.description: Exact mirror of foundation identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/scope-descriptor: the foundation record is the AUTHORITY and this document restates it field-for-field, including every array's owning x-opensip-order. wrapper.scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of this record (the same producing rule as plan.scopeDigest); retained as a blob. There is no separate workflow import-scope domain. Because one digest preimage is admitted through both documents, they must admit and refuse exactly the same bytes; the mirror-drift check proves it rather than asserting it.

Imported1ImportWrapperV2.description: Exact mirror of foundation import descriptor fields (schemaVersion 2). Every auxiliary digest is a raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of an exact closed record retained as a blob (identity-and-evidence §2 auxiliary-digest rule); none is an H(domain) identity: payloadSchemaDigest = raw SHA-256 of the exact registered schema DOCUMENT bytes (PayloadRegistryV1 row); payloadDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes; sourceCorrespondenceDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical common#SourceCorrespondence; buildDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical BuildIdentityV1; scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportScopeDescriptor (= foundation scope-descriptor); observationDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportObservationV1. importId = 'import2:' + H('import', this object) is the only H-domain identity in an import. No hidden metadata: every field is one of these thirteen.

Imported1ImportedEvidenceRecordV1.description: Operational custody record joining the wrapper, its payload binding, the resolved correspondence and staleness for a given Plan. Only importId enters the Plan (plan.importIds).

Imported1PayloadBinding.description: Closed table row: which registered payload schema each import kind admits and which contract owns the payload semantics.

payloadDomain.description: ONE registry, five rows: runtime/test/history admit ONLY the workflow payload domains (native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history adapter grammars are normalized by native into these payloads BEFORE import and are not import payload domains); dependency/prepared admit ONLY native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1 / native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1 (native-evidence.md §7 spellings).

schemaDocument.description: the registered schema DOCUMENT whose exact complete bytes hash to payloadSchemaDigest (raw SHA-256 of the file bytes; no canonical-schema hash exists)

selector.description: JSON pointer of the payload $def inside schemaDocument; the selector identifies the definition, the digest binds the document bytes

Imported1PayloadRegistryV1.description: The one closed import payload registry. Exactly these five rows exist; any other (kind, payloadDomain) pair is IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH and a domain with no row is IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED.

Imported1Root.title: Imported evidence: one foundation import2 wrapper, typed payloads as content (PROPOSED, revised)
Imported1Root.description: Import is an operational admission step (import custody), never an analysis Run. There is exactly ONE import identity: importId = H('import', foundation import descriptor) from foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/import (schemaVersion 2). The typed payload records here (runtime, test, history) and native's typed records (dependency-source, prepared-output, and native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history payload grammars) are PAYLOADS: their bytes are referenced by payloadDigest (raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes) and their registered schema by payloadSchemaDigest. The wrapper's identity therefore differs from the payload content hash, and one payload can appear under two wrappers only if correspondence/producer/adapter/scope also agree, which is the intended meaning. Hostile-input bounds: artifact at most 268435456 bytes; at most 1048576 subjects; at most 4096 blobs; JSON depth at most 32; strict UTF-8, no duplicate keys, no float lexemes, no surrogates. Observed no-hits during one window are never universal non-use; only observable-unhit subjects may be consumed by a predicate, and only with the window/population disclosed.

x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.standing: Normative and closed. A policy atom may name a relation from exactly two places: the thirteen NATIVE fact relations closed by foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry, or the imported-evidence relations below. An atom naming anything else refuses at policy admission; there is no open relation namespace and no default.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.why: Atoms range over imported-evidence subjects as well as native facts, and the same per-relation ladder law must decide their minResolution. Without a ladder for these relations the atom's rung is undecidable, which is the other half of the withdrawn abstract-tier vocabulary. These relations are deliberately NOT added to the native fact registry: they mint no fact2, they carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse, and that registry stays closed at thirteen.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.ladderRule: Same law as native relations: the ladder is that relation's own total order, weakest-first, and minResolution must be a member of it. Nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.rungVocabulary: No new rung token is introduced. `observed` is already the registered rung of the native `unresolved-edge` relation, and an import carries exactly one strength of claim: the observation was made. Window, population, observability and completeness are carried by the payload and the closed-world machinery, never by the rung.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.evidenceDeclarationRule: An atom naming one of these relations MUST carry `evidence` equal to that relation's evidenceKind, and its rule must declare a matching evidenceUse. An atom naming a native fact relation MUST NOT carry `evidence`. This keeps the two planes separable at admission rather than by convention.

x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.standing: Normative and CLOSED. THE outcome law for a repair EvidenceRequirement whose relation is one of the two imported-evidence relations registered above. It adds no relation, no rung, no import kind, no payload domain and no D9 class, code or exit.
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.whyItIsOwed: repair.schema.json#/$defs/EvidenceRequirement admits ANY relation that repair_preview's admit_atom admits, which is the thirteen native fact relations OR the two relations in this registry. Native section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2` ranges only over a native VIEW: asked about runtime-observation or history-change it returns `required-relation-missing`, because there is no view entry for a relation that mints no fact2. So a requirement over an imported relation was admissible with no defined producer for its outcome, and the earlier claim that sufficiency_v2 is the ONLY producer of that field was wrong for exactly these two relations.
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.twoPlanesOneField: The planes are NOT merged. A native requirement carries a DeficiencyV2 member; an imported requirement carries a member of this vocabulary. They are different sets because they name different machinery: DeficiencyV2 speaks of Coverage states, rungs, universes and resolution completeness, none of which an imported observation has. Writing `resolution-incomplete` about a runtime capture, or `import-unmapped-only` about a native view, is a category error and is refused. Which plane applies is decided at ADMISSION from the relation's registry membership - the same place the two planes are already separated by the evidenceDeclarationRule - and never guessed from the value.

evidence-kind-unavailable.meaning: No admitted import of this relation's evidenceKind reaches this Run.
evidence-kind-unavailable.boundTo: the admitted import set of the evidence Run named by RepairPlanDescriptor.evidenceRunId
evidence-kind-unavailable.groundedIn: section 5: an atom over imported evidence must be declared in evidenceUse and REQUIRED evidence absent makes the rule indeterminate.

import-unmapped-only.meaning: An import of the kind exists but is unmapped-only for this Plan.
import-unmapped-only.boundTo: the StalenessRule disposition of that import against this Plan
import-unmapped-only.groundedIn: section 4 StalenessRule: snapshot-differs, commit-differs, commit-equal-dirty and build-identity-differs are unmapped-only, and unmapped-only evidence never feeds a predicate. Explicitly SELECTING a stale import stays the separate IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN request refusal and is not this outcome.

subject-not-observable.meaning: A required target is carried by the runtime payload as `unobservable` or `unmapped`, so the capture made no claim about it in either direction.
subject-not-observable.groundedIn: section 4: unobservable/unmapped never become unhit signals and the schema refuses a hit count on them.

observation-window-insufficient.meaning: A mapped observation exists but its window or population does not meet what the recipe asked for.
observation-window-insufficient.boundTo: RuntimePayloadV1.observationWindow and observedPopulation, compared against the admitted repair recipe's declared demand; the demand is an input, never inferred from the payload
observation-window-insufficient.groundedIn: section 4: positive and bounded-negative runtime evidence is admitted always together with the observation window and population.

history-range-insufficient.meaning: A mapped history import exists but its revision range does not meet what the recipe asked for, or the range was truncated.
history-range-insufficient.groundedIn: HistoryPayloadV1 carries revisionRange with an explicit `truncated` flag and NO observationWindow, observedPopulation or observability. History has its own projection and the runtime one is never applied to it.

history-outside-collection-scope.meaning: A required target lies outside the scope the history collection covered, so its absence from the payload carries no information.
history-outside-collection-scope.groundedIn: collectionScope is a required member precisely so that an absent path can be distinguished from an unexamined one.

import-absent-for-requirement.meaning: The kind is available and consumable and the target was in scope, but the payload carries no subject row reaching that target.
import-absent-for-requirement.groundedIn: the existing IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE condition, applied per requirement rather than per predicate. Named separately from evidence-kind-unavailable because the remedies differ: import the evidence versus widen the capture.

x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.precedenceRule: Most specific first, in the order a consumer can act on: an absent kind is imported, an unmapped-only import is re-mapped or re-captured against the current snapshot, an unobservable subject is instrumented, an insufficient window is widened, and only then is the observation genuinely silent about the target. Every applicable condition is evaluated; the reported outcome is the first in this order.
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.whatThisOutcomeNeverEstablishes: No imported observation establishes a universal negative. One window never establishes universal non-use, `observable-unhit` is not `unused`, and runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. In particular imported evidence can NEVER BY ITSELF establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe delete or replace: EVERY delete and EVERY replace is decided against the evidence Run's own native ClosedWorldV2 (native section 4.5) before any descriptor exists, and no imported outcome changes deadCodeRepairEligible. It may, however, be an ADDITIONAL required condition alongside an already-established native safety basis - a recipe may lawfully require both - so it is wrong to say imported evidence can never affect applicability. Both directions are held by controls: an unsafe plan whose only requirement is a satisfied imported one is still refused by the closed-world gate, and an unsatisfied imported requirement still makes an otherwise-eligible plan inapplicable.
whatIsPreserved: the original evidence Run named by evidenceRunId remains the authority; nothing here is a substitute for it
per-target evaluation: the outcome is decided against THIS requirement's targets, not against the payload as a whole
observation window and observed population travel with every positive and bounded-negative claim, exactly as section 4 requires
required versus optional stays where evidenceUse already puts it; an optional absence is the existing IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE disclosure and is not a deficiency
the native sufficiency guard is untouched: sufficiency_v2 still owns every native relation and is not asked about these two
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.enforcedAt: workflows_model.admit_evidence_requirement decides the plane and refuses a cross-plane value or a shape violation at the repair-preview producer/consumer boundary; workflows_model.imported_requirement_outcome is the reference projection implementing the precedence and the per-kind applicability above, over already-admitted inputs. The vocabulary is mirrored into workflows common as ImportedRequirementDeficiency and held equal to this law.

perKindApplicability.rule: Each relation may report only the outcomes its own payload can ground. A history requirement can never report a runtime observability or window outcome, and a runtime requirement can never report a history range or collection-scope outcome; the producer refuses rather than borrowing the other kind's projection.

inputBinding.standing: EvidenceRequirement carries only relation, minResolution, completeness, satisfied and deficiency. Every other input this law reads is named here with the field that owns it, so no untyped caller value stands in for a measured Run.
inputBinding.targets: RepairPlanDescriptor.targets - the plan's own FINGERPRINTS. They are not a field of EvidenceRequirement and none is added. They are not payload subject keys either: see targetSubjectProjection for the deterministic join through the evidence Run's retained finding and its finding-fingerprint subjectKey, including symbol-versus-file granularity, the disclosed history widening, ambiguity refusal and unmatched handling.
inputBinding.allVersusAny: RepairPlanDescriptor.evidenceRequirements[].completeness. SELECTED CLARIFICATION, and its provenance is recorded accurately: the enum `complete | partial-acceptable` already existed, but its meaning FOR AN IMPORTED REQUIREMENT OVER PLAN TARGETS is chosen here and was not previously published. `complete` requires EVERY target supported; `partial-acceptable` requires at least one. An earlier revision said the enum `already means exactly this`, which was a historical overclaim.
inputBinding.requiredVersusOptional: the owning rule/recipe evidenceUse declaration (workflows section 5), projected by the host into a TYPED BOOLEAN input. The reference REFUSES a non-boolean rather than treating a falsy value as optional, so there is no `unknown` state at this boundary and no default is applied to one. An earlier revision claimed unknown declarations are read as required while accepting None and 0 as optional; the claim is withdrawn and the boundary is typed instead. A repair requirement is NOT automatically identical to policy predicate truth: the policy evaluator's optional-absence route is its own, under its own stated conditions, and this projection is related to the owning declaration rather than equated with that route.
inputBinding.windowDemand: The bounded observation demand is owned by the ADMITTED RECIPE CLOSURE named by RepairPlanDescriptor.recipe.closureId - a content-addressed, signed contribution closure whose current-trust disposition repair preview already resolves and whose revocation already invalidates apply. It is NOT a wire field: RecipeRef carries only contributionId, recipeId, recipeVersion and closureId, and an earlier revision wrongly spoke of `the admitted repair recipe's declared observation demand` as though such a field existed. The host projects the closure-owned deterministic demand into the typed input this reference consumes; the reference does not re-derive it and does not invent one when it is absent.
inputBinding.admittedInputsOnly: This is a PURE reference projection over inputs an authenticated importer and the retained Run closure have ALREADY admitted. It does not itself validate an opaque Run, does not re-derive source correspondence, and does not admit payload, observation scope or polarity - those remain the importer's and the evaluator's. Its preconditions are stated so a caller cannot mistake it for that admission.

x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.whatASatisfiedOutcomeMeans: It means the requirement's evidential condition was met over the BOUND window, range and population - not that the evidence is positive. `observed-hit` is positive execution evidence and `observable-unhit` is BOUNDED NEGATIVE evidence; both can satisfy a requirement, and which one did is carried in the disclosure rather than collapsed. An OPTIONAL absence that satisfies under the evidenceUse rule is satisfied by ABSENCE, not by positive evidence, and its disclosure says so. Calling every satisfied outcome positive would contradict section 4 and would throw away the richer evidence the bounded-negative case exists to carry.

targetSubjectProjection.standing: Normative and CLOSED, and a SELECTED CLARIFICATION rather than a restatement: nothing before this published how a repair target reaches an imported payload subject. It introduces no new record and no new field; it names the retained records that already carry the join.
targetSubjectProjection.theProblemItSolves: RepairPlanDescriptor.targets are FINGERPRINTS - `finding-key2:<64 hex>` - while RuntimeSubject is keyed by {path, symbol?} and HistorySubject by {path}. They are different vocabularies, and an earlier revision read the payload maps DIRECTLY by the target string and called the targets the payload subjects. That silently equated a finding-key identity with a LogicalPath and skipped a real join.
deterministicProjection: 1. TARGET -> FINDING. Every target must be a finding of the evidence Run named by RepairPlanDescriptor.evidenceRunId; repair preview already refuses a target that is not (REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED, `target fingerprint not in the evidence Run`). This is the binding to the ORIGINAL evidence Run and it is not weakened here.

2. FINDING -> FINGERPRINT DESCRIPTOR. The `finding-key2` identity is the H identity of the retained foundation `finding-fingerprint` descriptor, whose retention mode is `preimage`, so its exact bytes are retained under that digest and are re-hashed at Run closure. The projection therefore reads a RETAINED record, never a caller assertion.

3. DESCRIPTOR -> SUBJECT KEY. The retained descriptor carries subjectKey = {language, kind, logicalPath, qualifiedName, discriminator}. The projection reads logicalPath and qualifiedName for payload matching and reports the answer granularity; it does not classify the target using the open kind vocabulary.

4a. RUNTIME MATCH. A RuntimeSubject row matches when its `path` equals `subjectKey.logicalPath` AND, when that row carries `symbol`, its `symbol` equals `subjectKey.qualifiedName` - so a symbol-keyed row for a DIFFERENT symbol never matches. A row with NO symbol is a FILE-level observation: it matches on path but its answerGranularity is `file` and granularityWidenedToFile is true, so a path-only row NEVER silently passes as a symbol-level answer.
4b. HISTORY MATCH. HistorySubject has NO symbol field, so a row matches when its `path` equals `subjectKey.logicalPath`, and every history answer is file-level and reported as such.
5. AMBIGUITY REFUSES. If more than one payload subject matches one target, the projection is not deterministic and the host REFUSES rather than choosing; no silent first-match.
6. UNMATCHED IS UNSUPPORTED. A target with no matching subject is unsupported. It never becomes satisfied, and it is never read as evidence of non-use.
targetSubjectProjection.whatItDoesNotDo: It derives no fact, mints no identity, and admits no payload. It is a READ over records the authenticated importer and the retained Run closure have already admitted, and its result is the already-admitted projection the reference outcome function consumes.
targetSubjectProjection.referenceProjection: workflows_model.project_targets_to_imported_subjects implements steps 1-6 over the retained records and returns the per-target projection that imported_requirement_outcome consumes, so the join is EXERCISED and joined to its caller rather than only described. It refuses `native.imported-projection-ambiguous-target` and `native.imported-projection-target-not-in-evidence-run`.
targetSubjectProjection.granularityIsReportedNotClassified: Every subjectKey carries a qualifiedName, and `subjectKey.kind` has NO closed vocabulary in this contract set, so this projection does NOT classify the target by kind and no kind vocabulary is invented for it. What it reports is the granularity of the ANSWER relative to the key: `answerGranularity` is `symbol` only when a symbol-naming row matched, and `granularityWidenedToFile` marks every file-level answer to a keyed subject. Any coarsening the imported format cannot avoid - history having no symbol field at all, and a runtime capture that emitted only file rows - is therefore stated on the outcome rather than absorbed. This projection adds no capability to either payload format. A symbol-naming row represents only the imported format's path-and-name granularity: neither imported format distinguishes subjectKey.language, kind or discriminator. Different findings may therefore project to the same observation. This uniform projection limitation does not establish execution or non-execution of a particular subject variant beyond the captured granularity; answerGranularity=symbol is not an exact match of the complete subject key.

Imported1RuntimePayloadV1.description: Payload domain workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1. Its raw canonical bytes hash to wrapper.payloadDigest.

subjects.description: sorted strictly ascending by (path, symbol) UTF-8 bytes

observability.description: unobservable: the capture could not observe this subject (no source map, not instrumented); unmapped: no correspondence to an inventoried source path. Neither is ever an unhit signal.

Imported1SourceMappingV1.description: The one closed mapping artifact that makes vcs-revision/declared-build evidence consumable. Producing recipe: the adapter that generated the runtime/test artifact emits, for every generated path it observed, the digest of the generated bytes and the digest and path of the snapshot source it was built from; the host admits the mapping only when every sourceSha256 equals the snapshot2 inventory digest of sourcePath (else IMPORT.SOURCE_MAPPING_REQUIRED and the evidence stays unmapped-only). Digest: raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, retained as a blob and carried in SourceCorrespondence.sourceMappingDigest.

entries.description: sorted ascending by generatedPath; generatedPath unique

Imported1StalenessRule.description: Closed decision table row for staleness classification relative to a Plan's snapshot binding.

condition.description: commit-equal-clean-mapped: commit equal, clean, and an admitted SourceMappingV1 joins every generated path to the Plan snapshot by digest → current/consumable. commit-equal-clean-unmapped: commit and clean flag alone → current/unmapped-only (a commit string cannot prove byte correspondence).

owner.description: the contract that owns the command's semantics; the workflow inventory only enumerates and joins

grammarStanding.description: Candidate declared syntax; does not establish independent acceptance of the complete surface.

authorizationClass.description: what authorizes the command's effect (distinct from advisory, which describes its OUTPUT standing). none: read-only or ordinary durable write under the project writer. user-consent: interactive confirmation or --yes-policy. policy-record-or-consent: CI needs a pre-existing policy record. security-grant: an admitted RepoExecutionGrantV2. recovery-authority-quorum: an epoch signed by recoveryAuthority keys at its threshold (S4.5); ordinary root keys do not count. exclusive-lease: EXCLUSIVE lease (S7) plus explicit invocation. core-transition-leases: installation fence plus the S7 affected namespace EXCLUSIVE set, derived from the admitted intent and installation registry; same-schema core update/repair require the fence alone.

advisory.description: true: every output is Map-side and can never be a Control verdict or repair authorization

parityFields.description: fields whose value must be semantically identical across every applicable renderer of this command

writesTrackedIntent.description: true only for explicit policy-init/waive/baseline-adopt/baseline-export/baseline-upgrade; no other command writes a tracked file

firstSourceWrite.description: true when the command may perform the first source-derived write into the private store; such a command must carry the --allow-backup-custody join (identity §5 / TM V17)

Native2CanonicalRelativeDirV1.description:
INTERNAL relative DIRECTORY form: one or more slash-joined non-empty segments, no leading or trailing slash, no empty segment, no "." or ".." segment, no NUL and no backslash. Segments are decided by SPLITTING ON "/" and testing EXACT equality, which is the decision procedure the house already implements identically in two independent places: foundation/identity-model.v3.py `ordered()` (rejects a leading "/", a backslash, a NUL and any segment in ["", ".", ".."] for every `path`/`logicalPath` string) and discovery-defaults.py `normalize_explicit_root()` (same four tests over `spec.split("/")`). The negative test is therefore attached PER SEGMENT and ends with a strict end-of-input assertion rather than "$": "$" also matches before a trailing newline, and a ".*"-prefixed lookahead does not cross a newline at all, so a single whole-string lookahead both accepts "a
/../b" (an exact ".." segment) and rejects "a/.
" (whose final segment is ".
", not "."). No character beyond "/", backslash and NUL is excluded, because the owning grammar excludes none: a literal newline or other non-dot character inside a segment stays admissible. The declarative at-most-255-characters-per-segment bound of #/$defs/LogicalPath is deliberately NOT imported here; identity-schemas.v3 records it as a different, explicitly non-equivalent enforcement that reaches only two Blob path fields, and neither `ordered()` nor `normalize_explicit_root` imposes it. CanonicalPath is deliberately NOT this grammar: it admits a trailing slash and an interior empty segment ("a//b"), neither of which is canonical for a directory used as a membership prefix. The project root is NOT spelled here; see InternalUnitRootV1.

Native2NativeCause.description: The typed cause carried beside a DeficiencyV2 in a Coverage entry. Native2ResolutionCompletenessState.description: Which member is legal on a given entry is decided by RC-1 (native-evidence.md section 4.3) and is NOT schema-decidable: applicability is total over the registered (relation, rung) pairs and turns on membership of the RUNG in the closed five-member resolved set (resolved-target, resolved-binding, resolved-callee, checked, from-resolved-calls), never on the relation ladder length. A resolved rung must never be not-applicable - reachability@from-resolved-calls is a one-rung relation whose single rung IS resolved - and every other registered rung, including unresolved-edge@observed and types@annotated as well as the syntactic rungs, is not-applicable with attempted=false, unresolvedEdgeCount=0 and unresolvedEdgeClasses=[]. RC-0 runs first and is relation-specific: the pair must be registered, meaning the rung is a member of THAT relation's own ladder, so unresolved-edge@enumerated is refused although both tokens are registered. That check and the not-applicable minting law (attempted false, count 0, empty class list) are enforced by coverage_bijection at the producer boundary AND again at retained Run closure, and they hold for a FACT-FREE entry over an empty examined scope. not-applicable is never a fallback for an unregistered pair. stageTerminal is deliberately not constrained: a not-applicable entry may retain the stage terminal its producer observed.

Native2ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1.description: The retained resolution read-set layout a TypeScript context commits to when nodeModulesInReadSet is true. One row per installed package DIRECTORY inside the project that the resolver may read: installPath is the project-relative directory as the resolver walks it, realPath is the project-relative directory after symlink/workspace-link resolution (equal to installPath when there is no link), and contentSha256 is the raw SHA-256 of that package directory manifest file bytes (its package.json) as RETAINED, joined by digest (the blobJoin on the native.context.typescript.v2 nested record, native-evidence section 2.2). A layout ROW is a package-directory resolution observation, not itself a snapshot inventory row. The FILES the analysis actually read inside a listed package directory ARE snapshot inventory rows (identity-and-evidence section 3 'What sourceInventory contains'; native-evidence section 1.4 U-4/U-4a): they have membership syntax-only / host-ignore-convention, are retained under their inventory digests, and Run closure joins each such row to the installPath or realPath of a row of this record, refusing SNAPSHOT_PRUNED_TREE_NOT_A_READ otherwise. Unread material in an installed dependency tree is never inventoried. This record commits package-directory granularity only: which files inside a listed package were read is a host TCB observation. Required inputs read from OUTSIDE the project root, such as compiler library files and the TypeScript standard library, stay in their owning toolchain and stdlib closures and are never snapshot paths. An earlier description said no inventory row could exist for files in these directories; that contradicted the selected read-set law and is superseded. Rows are strictly ascending and unique by installPath, so one layout has one spelling. nodeModulesLayoutDigest is the raw SHA-256 of C(this record); it is null exactly when nodeModulesInReadSet is false.

x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.standing: Normative and CLOSED. For every DeficiencyV2 member, WHICH retained field carries its cause and what that field must say. There is no default row: a deficiency with no row here is a registry defect and refuses. Nothing in this registry changes DeficiencyV2, NativeCause, UnresolvedEdgeKindV1, ClosedWorldV2, the public DomainDetailCode registry or any D9 class, code or exit; every carrier it names already exists and is already closed.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.whyItIsNeeded: native-evidence section 10 labels its second column `Cause (nativeCause)` and then fills three of its rows with values that are not NativeCause members: `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage` for `resolution-incomplete`, `exports-open, exports-unknown` for `external-consumers-unknown`, and `compiler-inferred present` for `derivation-policy-unmet`. Each refuses schema validation as a nativeCause (`'computed-member-access' is not valid under any of the given schemas`), so the only representable value was null - which the NativeCause description itself defines as `a disclosure was owed and not made`. Worse, nothing compared the pair to anything: on the frozen reference a `resolution-incomplete` entry carrying the unrelated but schema-valid `lockfile-missing`, or relabelled `capability-missing`, or a `derivation-policy-unmet` with an empty derivationKinds, or an `external-consumers-unknown` over `exportsClosed: closed`, each closed a Run. A cause vocabulary that nothing derives and nothing compares leaves the disclosure optional in practice - the same argument that added the three body-language-* members, carried through to the rest of the table.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.whyNotMoreEnumMembers: Adding NativeCause members was rejected on the merits, not for compatibility. `resolution-incomplete` has a genuinely SET-VALUED cause: an entry can exhibit up to all sixteen UnresolvedEdgeKindV1 classes at once, and a scalar cannot carry them, so enum members would either lose information or force an arbitrary pick - the multi-cause defect the finding names. x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.standing: Normative and CLOSED. THE authority for TypeScriptConfigGraphV1 node `kind`. The schema enum publishes the three admissible values; this law publishes which one each node's path takes, which the prose previously delegated to `the schema and native admission` while neither stated it. It adds no enum member, no field and no record.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.appliesTo: EVERY node of the retained graph - the selected entry AND every non-entry node reached through `extendsResolved`. There is no entry-only rule and no default for the rest. A non-entry node's kind affects no derived value (see derivedValueScope), which is exactly WHY it needed a published rule: nothing else pins it and it is still committed to the identity.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.rule: kind is a total function of `node.path` alone. Take the BASENAME - the final `/`-separated segment of the path - and compare it BYTE-EXACTLY against the closed table below. A match takes the table's value; anything else is `other`. Nothing else is consulted: not the file's content, not its position in the graph, not whether it is the entry, not the directory, and not any caller assertion.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.comparison: EXACT and case-SENSITIVE over the whole basename, on the UTF-8 bytes of the CanonicalPath as retained. No prefix, suffix, glob or stem matching; no case folding; no Unicode normalization beyond what CanonicalPath already requires; no extension-only test. `TSConfig.json`, `.tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.jsonc` are each `other`, and a host that lowercases the basename on a case-insensitive filesystem before comparing has produced a different graph and a different identity.

x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.derivedValueScope: `configOrigin` is derived from the SELECTED ENTRY node's kind only: `jsconfig` for a jsconfig entry, otherwise `tsconfig`, and `synthesized` exactly when there is no entry. So `other` and `tsconfig` both derive `tsconfig` at the entry, and a non-entry node's kind derives nothing at all. That is the whole reason this law is owed: `configOrigin` does NOT pin `kind`, so without a published rule two conforming hosts could disagree on a value that no derived field would ever contradict.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.identityConsequence: kind sits INSIDE the hashed record. `tsconfigGraphHash` is the raw SHA-256 of C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1); TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs REQUIRES it and the binding checks equality; the universe H identity is fact.sourceUniverse and subject-scope.sourceUniverse, hence fact2, scope2, coverage2, view2, evidence3, seal3 and run3. Native owner admission re-runs this over retained payloads at identity-model.v3.open_run_closure; complete replay is identity-model.v3.close_run. Two readings of one repository containing `tsconfig.build.json` would therefore mint two RunIds and defeat independent replay across machines - the same defect class the analysis-spec `capabilityId` vocabulary was closed for, and closed the same way: by naming the authority beside the field. The historical evaluator2 graph reached evidence2/seal2/run2; that is the historical counterexample, not a current qualified claim.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.whyExactAndNotThePrefixConvention: Both readings are natural and they disagree on real files, so one had to be chosen and written down. Exact basenames are chosen because `kind` records WHICH RECOGNIZED CONFIGURATION FILE this node is, not what a project chose to name a base; because the exact table is TOTAL, decidable from the retained path alone and identical on every filesystem, whereas a prefix rule would additionally have to decide `jsconfig.build.json`, an extensionless `tsconfig` and `tsconfig.jsonc`; and because it is the rule the selected model already derives, so publishing it changes no existing value. `other` is not a defect classification: it is the honest statement that this node's basename is neither recognized name, which is exactly what an explicitly selected custom-named configuration presents. NOTE ON SCOPE: this rationale is internal to this design. No claim is made here about what any external toolchain recognizes or what meaning it assigns to a filename convention; such a claim would be unverified from these bytes and is not needed to fix the reading.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.notARecognitionRule: This law decides the `kind` of a node ALREADY IN the retained graph. Which config file is SELECTED as the entry, and which markers make a workspace unit at all, are section 1.4 U-1 and the shared discovery rule; nothing here mints a node, a unit or a program.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model.typescript_config_graph_faults, which READS this table rather than restating it and reports `native.config-graph-kind-contradicts-path:<path>` for any node whose declared kind is not the derived one - so a relabelled entry, a relabelled base and an asserted `tsconfig` on `tsconfig.build.json` all refuse. ORDERING, precisely: typescript_universe_retained_input_faults computes the candidate C(record) digest and compares it to the universe's tsconfigGraphHash BEFORE it calls the graph faults, and both contribute to one fault list. So a candidate hash may well be computed; what never happens is ADMISSION - the universe is not admitted and no identity is accepted while any fault stands. The earlier wording `refuse before the graph digest is used` described the wrong boundary.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.driftScope: The MODEL and this table cannot drift, because the model reads this table rather than restating it, and a control holds the derived values against it. x-opensip-public-route-registry.originatingBoundaryLaw: admission-and-qualification section 1 fixes the actor/layer split: `Invalid external input is an admission rejection with the existing carrier's D9 code; an invalid host-generated internal layer is a host invariant fault.` The inherited d9-exit-contract.v1.14 completes it: nonAnalysisDerivation rule 2 puts authored-config errors and failed preconditions in request-rejected, rule 5 puts HOST failures in operational-failed, and axes.domainCondition distinguishes `host-fault` from `precondition-failed`. x-opensip-public-route-registry.aliasMapIsContextFree: Only a key whose public DETAIL is the same for EVERY origin may appear in public-detail-registry internalAliases, because that map is context-free. Two keys qualify and are aliased there: native.requested-capability-mode-not-selected -> PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED and native.release-capability-undeclared -> native.capability-unavailable. The origin-DEPENDENT keys deliberately are NOT in that map - a context-free alias cannot express `CONFIG.INVALID when configured, absent when the host produced it` - and the keys whose detail is absent need no alias because they never surface as a DomainDetailCode. An earlier revision claimed all 14 belonged there and that the edit was mechanical; both claims were wrong.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model public_termination_for derives the termination and validates it against the real StepTermination schema; the guards themselves emit only the internal key.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.possibleOriginsLaw: Every key declares the boundaries at which it CAN arise, and a derivation refuses any other. A release declaration is never a user's configuration and a configured capability is never the host's own authenticated release input, so a caller cannot launder one actor's fault into another's. An origin-INDEPENDENT key still has possible origins - what is independent is the resulting class and code, not who could have caused it.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.unsupportedTypedIsNotOnThisTable: An UNSUPPORTED-TYPED request is admitted and ANSWERED, never refused: the Run closes and its Coverage carries `unknown` with the deficiency the OWNING DERIVATION selects under the section 10 precedence. For a relation the admitted universe cannot serve at all - a compiler-free references request under syntax-only - that is language-tier-unsupported with capability-missing, and it OUTRANKS provider-unavailable. A capability the release merely did not declare available carries provider-unavailable with capability-missing only where no more specific deficiency applies, and a CANDIDATE-ONLY capability has no Coverage entry at all - its public route is the advisory native.capability-unavailable notice in CommandEnvelope.availability, whose complete ownership tuple is defined in section 1.4. An earlier revision stated the provider-unavailable pair here as THE outcome for both cases, which contradicted the precedence and the candidate-only distinction section 1.4 publishes. Neither case may be converted into an admission refusal.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.envelopeErrorsComposition: A kind=failure CommandEnvelope REQUIRES a nonempty `errors` array of DomainDetail, so `termination.domainDetail` being OPTIONAL does not complete the public failure surface: a route that lawfully leaves it absent still owes the envelope a detail. An earlier revision stopped at StepTermination admission, and a minimal failure envelope built from the externally-supplied and host-generated routes refused `errors is a required property`. failure_envelope_errors composes it: where the termination carries a detail the array is EXACTLY that detail, so the two surfaces can never disagree; where it does not, the route's own `envelopeDetail` supplies one. Every code used is a member of the closed public DomainDetailCode registry. Four members were ADDED there rather than borrowing an unrelated remedy - native.capability-spec-invalid, native.release-declaration-invalid, native.coverage-cause-unsupported and HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED - because `a supplied spec names an unregistered capability`, `the installed release declaration is malformed`, `the provider emitted an unsupported deficiency/cause pair` and `the host violated its own invariant` are four different things for a caller to do next. Reuse was taken wherever it was honest: external configuration keeps CONFIG.INVALID and a NOT-SELECTED cell keeps PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED. Before a Plan or Run exists no run envelope is fabricated - the failure envelope carries the termination, its errors and the request id, and nothing else.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.remedyKeyingConstraint: NORMATIVE MAINTENANCE CONSTRAINT on the remedy table, promoted here from a source comment so it is part of the published law rather than advice a reader may miss. PUBLIC_ROUTE_REMEDIES is keyed by PUBLIC CODE, not by internal key. Several keys route to one code - native.requested-capability-unregistered, native.requested-capability-mode-unregistered and native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple all reach CONFIG.INVALID under external-configuration, and all three reach native.capability-spec-invalid as the externally-supplied-spec envelope detail - so ONE string must remain true for EVERY key that reaches that code, and a key whose remedy would be a DIFFERENT next step may not simply reuse the code. THIS IS CURRENTLY SATISFIED, not merely intended: the two strings widened for the ownership tuple state both the unregistered-name condition and the one-row-per-tuple condition, and the default-construction path added later routes to the same key and is covered by the same two sentences plus HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED, which is true of a host emitting two rows for one cell. The structural alternative - keying the remedy by (code, internal key) - is deliberately NOT taken: it changes the shape of an existing table for a case honest sentences already cover, and no key in this composition needs it. What is owed instead is exact: adding a key that routes to an existing code obliges its author to check that code's remedy is a true next step for the new condition and to widen it or choose another code if it is not.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.subjectNormalization: The guards emit COLON-SUFFIXED refusal strings - native.requested-capability-unregistered:made-up-capability, native.coverage-cause-not-for-deficiency:input-closure-incomplete:capability-missing - so a normalizer matching the whole string would find no registered key. normalize_internal_key matches the LONGEST registered key followed by a colon and takes the remainder as the subject, which is what reaches DomainDetail.subject so a caller sees WHICH value was refused. A raw string matching no registered key REFUSES (native.public-route-key-unregistered) rather than passing through, as the public registry aliasRule requires of an unknown key; an origin a key cannot have refuses too (native.public-route-origin-not-possible).
x-opensip-public-route-registry.subjectBoundLaw: DomainDetail.subject is BoundedText (1024) while a refused VALUE can be far longer: a structurally valid languageMode may be 4096 characters, and the composed subject then reached 4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at termination.domainDetail.subject or errors[0].subject. bounded_subject elides: the registered KEY is preserved verbatim - it selects the code, the class and the origin - and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. UNITS, because the two operations differ: `raw` is the composed subject as an admitted UNICODE SCALAR STRING, and length and slicing count UNICODE CODE POINTS - what BoundedText's JSON Schema maxLength counts - not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units; the SHA-256 input is exactly raw encoded as UTF-8 with NO additional normalization, rendered as 64 lowercase hex characters after the ASCII marker `...#sha256:`, giving exactly 1024 code points. A non-ASCII value can therefore have a UTF-8 byte length above 1024 while its scalar length does not, and the two must not be conflated. GUARANTEE: distinct long values are distinguished under the ORDINARY COLLISION-RESISTANCE ASSUMPTION for SHA-256, not by any impossibility claim, and the guarantee is confined to what is PUBLISHED - the bounded subject and its digest. No separate retained store of the untruncated value is promised or named here; a host keeping its own operational log matches it by recomputing this digest. Emitting the untruncated string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and reclassifying the input error as success would be false; the code, class and origin are never changed by the elision.

x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.standing: Normative and CLOSED. The per-language capability mapping of the bundled grammar set, published here so a consumer can reconstruct it without reading author code. syntaxClass is NOT caller-selected: a grammar row declaring a class other than the one this registry assigns to its languageId is refused at grammar-bundle admission, in both directions.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.source: native_evidence_model.v2.BUNDLED_GRAMMARS (the same table the shared discovery rule uses for the grammar-only membership path) and native-evidence section 6.3.

classLaw.code: The language has the section 6.3 body spans - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L2/L3 normalisation table. Bears clone body identity (clones@normalized-body-hash) and the code-construct syntax relations (declares/literal/control-flow @ syntactic). Its languageId MUST be a member of foundation body-language-version.languageId, because that identifier enters the clone preimage.
classLaw.data-document: A bundled grammar for a data or document format. It has no section 6.3 body spans, and this kit publishes no tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law for it. Its files are grammar-only MEMBERS - accounted, inventoried, never unsupported-file - bearing file/package/vcs-change inventory evidence under the syntax universe. It mints NO body identity, no suffix of it appears in the syntax dialect table, and its languageId MUST NOT be in body-language-version.languageId. A clone or code-construct request against it is explicitly UNAVAILABLE (language-tier-unsupported for that capability), never a complete empty clone result, which would read as a finding of no clones.

x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.unbundledLanguages: A language with no bundled grammar is not representable here at all: its files are unsupported-file with reason no-bundled-grammar, and its languageId is outside the SyntaxGrammarBundleV1 vocabulary. Adding one is a deliberate registry change, not a caller choice.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.futureCapability: Data-format syntax facts (for example literal@syntactic over JSON or YAML) would require a published tokenisation and literalKind law. None exists in this kit, so the mapping above does not promise them. This is a bounded future capability, deliberately not invented here.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.enforcementBoundaries: This registry is the authority at THREE boundaries, not one. (1) Grammar-bundle admission: a row's declared syntaxClass must equal the registered one, in both directions. (2) Every admitted fact2 under a syntax universe: every ANCHOR PATH must be read by a SELECTED grammar whose capability set contains that relation@rung. (3) Every requested subject-scope under a syntax universe, INCLUDING an empty view: judged on the committed examined extent, where a code capability needs at least one extent path read by a selected code grammar, and a capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable. INVENTORY CAPABILITIES (file@enumerated, package@manifest-declared, vcs-change@vcs-reported) are ALWAYS available and are never grammar-gated at boundary (2) OR boundary (3). An earlier revision stated that exemption only inside boundary (3), and boundary (2) read as an unconditional every-anchor rule; a literal implementer therefore refused the very inventory facts boundary (3) had just promised were unconditionally available, which made an inventoried .py path inventoriable and unrepresentable at the same time. The exemption belongs to both because it is a property of the RELATION, not of the boundary: an inventory fact is not read by a grammar at all - it is the snapshot inventory row, the manifest declaration or the VCS observation - so there is no grammar for it to be gated on. Independently of this exemption the relation registry anchorLaw closes the inventory class at ZERO anchors, so an inventory fact names no anchor path for boundary (2) to test in the first place; the two laws agree and neither depends on the other. An earlier revision enforced only (1), which constrains what a bundle says about itself and not what a Run claims: Markdown declares facts, complete empty declares/clones Coverage and references@resolved-binding under resolutionAttempted=false all admitted. None of the three consults a claimed coverage value, a caller-declared class, or whether facts exist.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.unavailableRequestDisclosure: A well-formed request for a capability this universe cannot serve is DISCLOSED, not answered and not refused outright: coverage `unknown`, deficiency `language-tier-unsupported`, nativeCause `capability-missing` - existing vocabulary, mapped in native-evidence section 10. A false `complete`, a wrong or null cause and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own typed reason. The capability is retained: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar declares/clones Run still close with a genuine complete and no deficiency.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.selectionMatters: An UNSELECTED grammar lends no capability. Selection is committed in the universe identity, so a bundle that ships a grammar the universe did not select cannot make its capabilities available.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.inventoryIsNotGrammarGated: Normative. A snapshot inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads, so requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow the promise this registry makes. The three inventory capabilities are therefore exempt at every boundary this registry owns, on every path - unsupported suffix, extensionless, data-document and code alike - and a `vcs-change` on a `deleted` path that is not in the snapshot at all. This is an exemption from GRAMMAR OWNERSHIP only. It does not exempt an inventory fact from its relation's snapshot joins (path in the inventory; for `file` also the content digest, the byte length and custody of the retained bytes), from own-scope attribution, or from the anchorLaw; and it does not make a CODE fact admissible merely because some other anchor of the same Run is on a supported path.

x-opensip-digest-law.standing: The closing digest law of identity-and-evidence section 3, extended to this bundle. Every 64-hex or sha256: field here carries x-opensip-digest naming its representation, retention and authority. There is no default and no residue: a new field added without an annotation is inadmissible, exactly as in identity-schemas.v3.

retention.preimage: the exact preimage bytes are retained under this digest
retention.preimage-frame: the retained object is the H preimage frame, so SHA256(retained bytes) is the digest
retention.closure-tree-member: the digest must be a member digest of the retained signed closure tree the annotation names
retention.owner-retained: the named owning contract retains and admits the bytes; this bundle joins by digest equality
retention.derived: Recompute the identity from the retained owning record, with no separately retained preimage frame. In this bundle the three SourceUnitOwnershipV1 unitId positions resolve through units[]: derive H(native.compilation-unit.v1, UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion:1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName}) from the matching row and compare; selectedUnitIds and ownership[].unitId must name a row in that same closed table.

x-opensip-digest-law.siteCountLaw: Count syntactic x-opensip-digest annotation occurrences in this schema document; the reference checker reports the measured count. No second hand-maintained total is normative.

Native2RuntimeCoverageAdapterInputV1.description: INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was RuntimeCoveragePayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).

configProjectionSha256.description: The 64-hex suffix of H(native.cargo-config-projection.v2, CargoConfigProjectionV2) over the bound context configProjection record. A bare DigestHex, never a Sha256Text, and never the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes.

sourceUnitOwnershipId.description: Required and nullable, exactly as preparedOutputSetId is. null means NO committed ownership: such a universe admits no clones fact AT ALL, whatever its edition map looks like. An earlier revision of this description said null was admissible 'only while the edition map has a single distinct value, where every body has the same dialect and no owner selection arises'. That was the withdrawn package-default fast path and it is contradicted by the retained selectionLaw and by body_language_version, which refuses on missing ownership unconditionally: Cargo lets a target override its package default, so even a single-valued edition map can contain targets at different effective editions, and agreeing package defaults therefore never determine a body's dialect. The nullable form is retained deliberately - a universe whose ownership is unavailable or only partially enumerated is a legitimate retained universe; it simply mints no body identity, its clones Coverage carries the typed ownership disclosure (deficiency input-closure-incomplete with the matching body-language-* nativeCause), and its empty clone view stays indeterminate rather than becoming a finding of no clones.

Native2RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.description: executionCapableResolution=true means only that prepared products of some execution were consumed as inert data (preparedResolution != none). It is never a host execution grant; the grant is the operational RepoExecutionGrantV1 reference outside Plan.

Native2SourceUnitOwnershipV1.description: The committed relation from a SNAPSHOT SOURCE PATH to the compilation TARGET that reads it, the closed table of those targets, and the EXPLICIT SELECTION of which of them this universe analyses. It exists because a body span dialect is a property of the compilation target: neither a crate-name-to-root map nor the package edition map can supply it, since #[path], files shared by several targets and several compilation contexts of one crate defeat a directory inference, and Cargo lets a target override its package default edition. Because this record is committed by H identity inside RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId, a different SELECTION is a different record, a different identity and therefore a DIFFERENT sourceUniverse: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is validly analysed under each, one selection at a time, with no change to any relation payload. Every row is a retained native observation; nothing here executes Cargo, a build script or a repository read, and nothing here qualifies a compiler or an enumerator.

enumeration.description: complete: every compiled source path OF THE SELECTED UNITS has a row, so a path with no row is not compiled by any selected target. partial: the producer did not finish, so an owner INSIDE the selected scope may exist that is not listed. These are different claims and the second is not a weaker form of the first: an unlisted owner could contradict a listed one, so no clone body dialect is admissible under partial. That is checked BEFORE any row lookup, so partial discovery can never act as an implicit edition selection by hiding a conflicting owner. Partial evidence remains useful under the existing facts and Coverage law: the clones scope reports its incompleteness and the predicate is indeterminate, rather than a body identity being minted on an unbounded claim.

units.description: The closed table of compilation targets. Strictly unique by unitId, and unitId is a FUNCTION of the metadata, so two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal rather than two units that differ by accident. A selection or an ownership row naming a unitId with no row here is an unbound caller label and is inadmissible.

unitId.description: H(native.compilation-unit.v1, UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion:1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName}) over the very fields this row carries. DERIVED retention: nothing separate is retained because the preimage IS the row, and admission re-derives and compares (sourceUnitOwnership.unitId). Not an opaque digest - preimage record, domain and selector are all published - and not a delimiter label, which could stay injective only by narrowing admitted repository paths.

markerPath.description: The inventoried manifest that declares this target: the same markerPath vocabulary WorkspaceUnitV2 already uses, cited rather than duplicated. WorkspaceUnitV2 and UnitMembershipV1 identify WORKSPACE units - cargo-package and cargo-workspace - which is the wrong granularity here, because one package holds several targets that may carry different editions; naming the marker joins the two rather than competing with them.

crateName.description: A key of the universe edition map, which supplies the package default.

targetEdition.description: The target's OWN edition when it sets one, null when it takes the package default. Cargo documents edition on a target as well as on a package: cargo-metadata lists targets[].edition and states the package edition is a DEFAULT individual targets may differ from. null DEFERS to the universe edition map for crateName, so the two committed places can never contradict: an override is explicit and visible, and its absence is explicit too.

selectedUnitIds.description: The EXPLICIT analysis scope: the compilation targets this universe analyses. Every member must be a unitId of the units table. This is what makes a shared path representable at two editions without an ambiguous claim - two selections are two universes - and it is what distinguishes SELECTED SCOPE from INCOMPLETE ENUMERATION. An owner outside the selection is deliberately out of scope and its edition does not bear on a body; an unlisted owner INSIDE the selection is a gap in knowledge and refuses. Silently omitting a conflicting owner from the units table is not a selection: the omission is invisible, whereas a selection is committed in the identity.

ownership.description: The pure relation. It carries no edition and no metadata, so it cannot contradict the units table.

Native2SubjectScopeCommitmentV1.description: The producing result for the retained c2-plan-stage-schema.v4 coverage key field. subjectScopeCommitment is the SAME 64 hex as the foundation subject-scope identity scopeId, re-spelled in the native Sha256Text text form; it introduces no second preimage and no native H domain.

Native2SyntaxGrammarBundleV1.description: The installed, closure-bound grammar bundle that a syntax-only analysis parses with. It is the component that INTERPRETS a body span in that mode, so it is pinned exactly the way a toolchain is: closureId names an admitted kind=grammar closure, parserVersion must equal that closure manifest's semanticVersion (admission refuses native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest otherwise, mirroring the compiler-version rule), and bundleDigest is the exact retained bundle identity. `grammars` is the CLOSED bundled-grammar set: it is what native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' actually denotes, and what makes `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` decidable rather than a matter of taste.

parserName.description: The component that reads the body span. Not a compiler: a syntax-only universe executes none, and naming one here would claim an interpretation that never happened.

languageId.description: Every language the host actually bundles a grammar for, matching BUNDLED_GRAMMARS exactly. An earlier revision listed only typescript/javascript/rust and claimed equality with the body-language-version enum as a drift check; that could not express the four data/document grammars the host has always bundled, so native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' was unrepresentable for them. What is actually held equal to the body-language-version enum is the set of languages whose grammars are syntaxClass=code - see syntaxClass.

syntaxClass.description: Which capability this grammar's files bear, and the exact distinction the original contracts already draw. `code`: the language has the body spans native-evidence section 6.3 defines - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L1-L3 normalisation table, so its files can bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations. Its languageId MUST be a member of the foundation body-language-version languageId enum, because that identifier goes into the clone preimage. `data-document`: a bundled grammar for a data or document format with no such body spans and no published tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law anywhere in this kit. Its files are grammar-only members - accounted, never `unsupported-file` - and bear inventory evidence (file/package/vcs-change); they mint no body identity, and its languageId MUST NOT be in the body-language-version enum, since it can never appear in a clone preimage. Claiming code-construct syntax facts for a data format would require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, which is exactly the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to avoid.
